summary: JIT env bootstrap fails when AWS STS session policy exceeds account enforced length; ephemeral SA not provisioned
description:
Issue summary: Automatic just-in-time (JIT) environment bootstrap jobs that create ephemeral AWS credentials for ML debugging fail intermittently in prod-us-east. The provisioner attempts to attach a generated STS session policy (inline session policy) that enumerates allowed S3 prefixes and KMS key ARNs. When the generated policy exceeds ~2048 characters, AWS STS call returns AccessDenied or MalformedPolicy depending on account policy enforcement, and the ephemeral service account creation aborts.

Impact: Developer oncall and data-platform jobs cannot spin up ephemeral sandboxes; several debugging and oncall plays blocked since 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Affects ~12 recent bootstrap attempts across two tenant projects. No user data exfiltration observed; primarily availability impact.

Environment: prod account (redwood-prod-ml), region us-east-1, provisioner v1.12.4, sts-provisioner lambda in us-east-1.

Observed behavior: STS:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and AssumeRole with SessionPolicy fails when inline sessionPolicy body length > ~2048 characters. Error surfaced to caller as HTTP 403 AccessDenied with message referencing policy validation or as 400 MalformedPolicy in some runs. Logs show policy string truncated in policy serializer before signing.

Expected behavior: JIT bootstrap should gracefully fall back to a role-based allow-list or use a smaller session policy (or create a short-lived role with attached managed policy) so ephemeral SA provisioning completes.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger JIT bootstrap via /internal/provisioner API for tenant project 'tenant-42' with full dataset access scope (S3 prefixes list ~35 entries).
Provisioner generates an inline sessionPolicy JSON that enumerates every S3 prefix and KMS key resource ARN and calls STS AssumeRole with sessionPolicy.
Observe the STS API error in CloudTrail and the provisioner lambda logs showing 403 AccessDenied or 400 MalformedPolicy.
Re-run with a reduced set of S3 prefixes (e.g., 3 prefixes) and observe successful AssumeRole and ephemeral credentials returned.
logs: 2026-03-09T22:04:12Z provisioner ERROR assume-role failed: AccessDenied: The session policy is invalid or exceeds allowed size (status 403)
2026-03-09T22:04:12Z aws-sdk DEBUG STS.AssumeRole request payload length=2764
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:00 - Reproduced locally by generating policy with 35 S3 prefixes; failure surface identical to prod logs.

03/10 10:15 - Checked org SCPs and IAM permission boundaries. No explicit deny on sessionPolicy content found, but account-level policy length enforcement appears active via account guardrails (security tooling may truncate or reject long inline policies).

03/10 11:05 - Observed serializer truncation in provisioner v1.12.4 when policy length close to 2048; older v1.11.0 did not include verbose resource enumeration and succeeded for same request size (confirmed by A/B).

03/10 13:40 - Ran targeted test swapping inline sessionPolicy for AssumeRole with role sessionName only (no sessionPolicy) -> succeeded, but opens a larger resource surface if we broadly attach managed role.

03/11 08:30 - Hypothesis: security account proxy strips or enforces limits on session policy length; combined with our verbose resource-by-resource policy generation, total payload triggers rejection.
comments: Olivia Chen (Support) 2026-03-10T09:12: Created ticket after multiple oncall reports. Captured batch of failed bootstrap IDs and initial logs.

Marcus Patel (SRE) 2026-03-10T10:20: Investigating. Running repro in staging with same provisioner binary. Initial findings point to policy length. Will try a fallback that collapses resource lists into prefix patterns.

Aisha Rahman (Security) 2026-03-10T11:02: Noted that a recent org hardening change introduced a Service Control Policy that rejects certain inline policy characteristics in sessions. Coordinating with cloud infra to confirm.

Marcus Patel (SRE) 2026-03-11T14:45: Temporary mitigation deployed to prod: provisioner now detects >=1200 char sessionPolicy and instead issues AssumeRole without sessionPolicy plus a short-lived managed role mapping with narrowly scoped permissions. This reduces blast radius while restoring bootstrap success. Monitoring metrics show successful bootstrap rate increased from 63% -> 98% over the last 6 hours.
Olivia Chen (Support) 2026-03-11T15:05: Notified impacted teams and updated incident channel #internal-support with workaround instructions.
resolution: Workaround applied: provisioner update (v1.12.5) implements a policy-size check. When generated sessionPolicy exceeds threshold, provisioner switches to 'role-alias' flow: create a short-lived managed role in the tenant shadow account and attach minimal managed policy (via automated role-allocator), then call AssumeRole without inline sessionPolicy. Follow-ups: (1) Security to confirm if org SCP can be relaxed for sessionPolicy length or allow policy-allocator service to attach managed role; (2) Engineering to ship a compact policy generator that uses prefix patterns instead of enumerating each resource; (3) Long-term: implement signed session policy storage (policy-refs) to keep STS payloads small or migrate to token-exchange with external OIDC flow. Incident will remain open until role-allocator infra change is vetted in canary.
next_steps: Security: validate org policy enforcement and either whitelist policy-allocator service or provide explicit guidance (target date 2026-03-14).
Engineering: merge compact-policy-generator PR and roll out v1.12.6 to prod canary (target date 2026-03-16).
SRE: implement additional metrics to track sessionPolicy lengths and rejection rates; add alert if >0.5% bootstrap failures in 1h window.
